warnings.detail: cross-doc drift [borrowed-invariants] -- BOOT.md must say `next_action` is the previous session's pre-computed pick and is confirmed against BOARD.md where the validator cannot re-derive it -- the portable floor does not, since a grep cannot walk a needs: graph

cross-doc drift [command-outranks-pick] -- BOOT.md step 7 must say the user's own message outranks `next_action` and defer to § 1.11's OBEY priority. Read as unconditional it is the half a cold agent reaches first, which is exactly how the command the user typed gets dropped

cross-doc drift [shortcut-memory-ban] -- BOOT.md step 7 must resolve a shortcut through the registry table before acting and explicitly state that memory is never a source for it. An agent that believes it knows what a key means answers from recall rather than reading the file
cross-doc drift [shortcut-memory-ban] -- BOOT.md step 7 must explicitly forbid duplicating the shortcut table into BOOT. A second copy drifts and defeats the read-the-source rule
cross-doc drift [chat-voice] -- BOOT.md no longer mandates STYLE.md (caveman-дед) before output. It governs every response from the first token, so deferring it to an escalation is too late

cross-doc drift [chat-voice] -- BOOT.md lost its '## Cold route' or '## Routing failures' heading; the cold-route STYLE.md read cannot be located, so the check fails loud instead of passing vacuously (T-405)
cross-doc drift [crew-naming] -- COMMANDS.md's `saipen crew` row is missing; the sequential circuit must be defined (T-571)

cross-doc drift [shortcut-semantics] -- cc:enters convergence from `normal`; cc:resumes `execution_intent: goal`; cc:never asks for an objective; cc:`cc <args>` is not a goal; gg:NEW GOAL ONLY; gg:`gg <objective>`; gg:never a continuation alias

CHANGELOG.md carries <n> while it states it keeps the most recent ~10 -- the overflow belongs in CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md, moved verbatim the way LOG segments are sealed, so the top of the file stays the part anyone actually reads

29 locale README(s) carry a source digest that no longer matches README.md's normalised content (ar, bg, cs, da, de, el, es, fi, fr, he, hi, hr, hu, id, it, ja, ko, nl, no, pl, pt, ro, sk, sv, th, tr, uk, vi, zh) -- the English prose moved and the translation did not follow. Version strings are normalised out, so a badge bump can never cause this
